metadata.description: FluidServe offline seed. decode_step_law gives the cost of a decode-only iteration as a function of the KV tokens held and the number of decoding requests. prefill_step_law gives the cost of an iteration that carries a prefill chunk. classes[] gives the empirical survival function of output length per SLO tier, used for the conditional completion probability. mixed_step_validation reports how well the mixture model reproduces measured window means, bucketed by the fraction of steps that carried a prefill chunk.
metadata.classes_note: classes[] rebuilt 2026-08-02 00:49 KST from runs after Agent_applications 5fa82f8 (2026-07-29 16:35 KST), which changed the deep research report structure from four sections to seven and took that class's median output from 249 to 942 tokens. The 2026-07-26 profile said mean 282 for a class measuring 951, so completionProb over the 100-iteration horizon read 0.355 against a true 0.105 and the release term of the KV projection was over-predicted by about 3.4x on the class holding roughly 77% of resident KV. decode_step_law and prefill_step_law are unchanged from the 2026-07-26 fit.
metadata.classes_superseded: the 2026-07-26 classes[] is kept beside this file as fluidserve-classes-20260726.json; nothing else in this document changed
metadata.flatlen_note: All three classes share one deterministic output length of 532 tokens, the mix-weighted mean of the 79,100 completed requests in 260831_2015_exp109r1_fsv3capgnofrct75_shift. This removes per-class length knowledge while keeping the tier keys (25/50/100) and the engine-side step laws unchanged, so the only thing ablated is the workload length model.
